name: Gaussian integral
derivation: Square the integral, write it as a double integral over the plane and change to polar coordinates, where it becomes ∫∫ e^{-r²} r dr dθ.
where_pi_enters: Integrating dθ from 0 to 2π in polar coordinates (the r integral gives ½).

name: Normal density normalizing constant
derivation: Require ∫φ = 1; substituting x = √2 u reduces ∫e^{-x²/2}dx to √2 times the Gaussian integral √π, so the constant is 1/√(2π).
where_pi_enters: Through the Gaussian integral, i.e. integrating dθ from 0 to 2π after passing to polar coordinates.

name: Total of the Cauchy kernel
derivation: The antiderivative is arctan x, so the integral is arctan(∞) − arctan(−∞).
where_pi_enters: ∫ dx/(1+x²) over the whole line: arctan runs from −π/2 to π/2.

name: Cauchy density coefficient
derivation: Normalize the kernel 1/(1+x²) by its total over the line.
where_pi_enters: Dividing by ∫ dx/(1+x²) over the whole line, which is π.

name: Basel problem
derivation: Compare coefficients of x² in the Taylor series of sin x / x and in its product over its zeros ±nπ (Euler), or Parseval for the Fourier series of x on [−π, π].
where_pi_enters: The zeros of sin x at x = nπ, so the product over them carries 1/(n²π²).

name: Zeta at 4
derivation: Parseval's identity applied to the Fourier series of x² on [−π, π], or the x⁴ coefficient of Euler's product for sin x / x.
where_pi_enters: The Fourier series on the interval [−π, π] (period 2π), whose norms carry powers of π.

name: Sum over odd reciprocal squares
derivation: Subtract the even terms ζ(2)/4 from ζ(2), leaving (3/4)·π²/6; or Parseval on the square wave's Fourier series.
where_pi_enters: Through ζ(2), i.e. the zeros of sin x at multiples of π.

name: Leibniz series
derivation: Integrate the geometric series 1/(1+t²) = Σ(−t²)ⁿ term by term from 0 to 1 (Abel's theorem at the endpoint).
where_pi_enters: ∫₀¹ dt/(1+t²) = arctan 1, a quarter of the half-turn.

name: Wallis product
derivation: Take the ratio of ∫₀^{π/2} sinⁿx dx for even and odd n via the reduction formula and let n → ∞; or evaluate Euler's product for sin x at x = π/2.
where_pi_enters: The even-power integrals ∫₀^{π/2} sin^{2m}x dx, which end on ∫₀^{π/2} dx = π/2.

name: Dirichlet integral
derivation: Write 1/x = ∫₀^∞ e^{-xt} dt, swap the integrals and integrate e^{-xt} sin x in x to get ∫₀^∞ dt/(1+t²).
where_pi_enters: ∫₀^∞ dt/(1+t²) = arctan(∞) = π/2.

name: Integral of sinc squared
derivation: Integrate by parts to reduce it to ∫ sin(2x)/x dx over the line, twice the Dirichlet integral; or Parseval with the box function.
where_pi_enters: Through the Dirichlet integral, ∫ dt/(1+t²) over a half-line.

name: Gamma of one half
derivation: Substituting t = x² turns ∫₀^∞ t^{-1/2} e^{-t} dt into 2∫₀^∞ e^{-x²} dx, the Gaussian integral.
where_pi_enters: The Gaussian integral, via integrating dθ over the full turn in polar coordinates.

name: Second Gaussian moment
derivation: Integrate by parts (or differentiate ∫e^{-ax²} = √(π/a)/2 in a) to reduce to the half-line Gaussian integral √π/2.
where_pi_enters: The Gaussian integral, via the polar-coordinates step over the full turn.

name: Fresnel integral
derivation: Rotate the contour of ∫ e^{ix²} dx by 45° in the complex plane, turning it into e^{iπ/4} times the half-line Gaussian integral, and take the real part.
where_pi_enters: The Gaussian integral √π/2 after the contour rotation.

name: Stirling's formula constant
derivation: Laplace's method on Γ(n+1) = ∫ tⁿ e^{-t} dt: expand the exponent to second order about t = n, leaving a Gaussian integral.
where_pi_enters: The Gaussian integral of the second-order expansion about the peak.

name: Area of the unit disc
formula: A = π r², with r = 1: π
derivation: Integrate r dr dθ over 0 ≤ r ≤ 1, 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π, or sum thin rings 2πr dr.
where_pi_enters: Integrating dθ from 0 to 2π (the r integral gives ½).

name: Circumference of the unit circle
derivation: Arc length ∫ √(x′² + y′²) dθ of (cos θ, sin θ) over one revolution.
where_pi_enters: Integrating dθ from 0 to 2π, the period of the circle's parametrization.

name: Volume of the unit ball
derivation: Stack discs of area π(1 − z²) for z from −1 to 1 (or integrate r² dr dΩ).
where_pi_enters: The area of each cross-sectional disc, π times its squared radius.

name: Surface area of the unit sphere
derivation: Integrate sin φ dφ dθ over 0 ≤ φ ≤ π, 0 ≤ θ ≤ 2π (Archimedes' hat-box: equal to the cylinder's lateral area).
where_pi_enters: Integrating dθ from 0 to 2π (the φ integral gives 2).

name: Area of the unit 3-sphere
derivation: Compute ∫_{ℝ⁴} e^{-|x|²} dx = π² two ways, as a product of four Gaussian integrals and in polar form |S³|·∫ r³ e^{-r²} dr = |S³|/2.
where_pi_enters: The fourth power of the Gaussian integral √π.

name: Volume of the unit 4-ball
derivation: Integrate the 3-sphere's area 2π² r³ from r = 0 to 1, or stack 3-balls of volume (4π/3)(1 − w²)^{3/2}.
where_pi_enters: Through the area of the unit 3-sphere, i.e. the Gaussian integral to the fourth power.

name: Buffon's needle
derivation: With the needle's angle θ uniform on [0, π) and its centre's distance uniform on [0, d/2], it crosses when the distance is below (l/2) sin θ; integrate.
where_pi_enters: Dividing by the length π of the uniform angle's range (the mean of sin θ over a half-turn is 2/π).

name: Coprime probability
derivation: The probability is ∏_p (1 − 1/p²) = 1/ζ(2) by the Euler product.
where_pi_enters: The value ζ(2) = π²/6 of the Basel problem.

name: Mean absolute value of a standard normal
derivation: Compute 2∫₀^∞ x φ(x) dx = 2/√(2π) directly, since x e^{-x²/2} has antiderivative −e^{-x²/2}.
where_pi_enters: The normalizing constant 1/√(2π) of the normal density.

name: Asymptotic efficiency of the median
derivation: The sample median's asymptotic variance is 1/(4n f(m)²); with f(m) = 1/√(2π σ²) it is πσ²/(2n), against the mean's σ²/n.
where_pi_enters: The normal density's height at its centre, 1/√(2πσ²).

name: Standard error of the median
derivation: Take the square root of the asymptotic variance 1/(4n f(m)²) with f(m) = 1/(σ√(2π)).
where_pi_enters: The normal density's height at its centre, 1/(σ√(2π)).

name: Arcsine law density
derivation: Normalize 1/√(x(1−x)); with x = sin²θ the integral becomes ∫₀^{π/2} 2 dθ. (Lévy's arcsine law for the time a random walk spends positive.)
where_pi_enters: Integrating 2 dθ from 0 to π/2 after the substitution x = sin²θ.

name: Wigner semicircle law
derivation: The moments method (Catalan numbers) for a Wigner matrix's spectrum gives the semicircle; normalize √(1 − x²) on [−1, 1].
where_pi_enters: The semicircle's area ∫ √(1 − x²) dx = π/2, half the unit disc.

name: Cauchy's formula for mean width
formula: mean width of a planar convex body = perimeter/π
derivation: The width in direction θ is the projection of the boundary, and averaging projections over directions gives (1/π)·∫|cos| times the perimeter, by Crofton's formula.
where_pi_enters: Averaging the projected length over the direction θ uniform on [0, π).

name: Full-wave rectified sine average
formula: mean of |sin ωt| over a period = 2/π
derivation: Average |sin θ| over one half-period: (1/π)∫₀^π sin θ dθ = 2/π.
where_pi_enters: Dividing by the half-period π of |sin θ|.

name: Square wave fundamental
formula: first Fourier coefficient of a ±1 square wave = 4/π
derivation: b₁ = (1/π)∫_{−π}^{π} sgn(sin x) sin x dx = (2/π)∫₀^π sin x dx = 4/π.
where_pi_enters: The Fourier coefficient's normalization 1/π over the period [−π, π].

name: Coulomb constant
derivation: Gauss's law ∮E·dA = q/ε₀ on a sphere about a point charge gives E·4πr² = q/ε₀.
where_pi_enters: The area 4πr² of the sphere surrounding the charge.

name: Field of a long straight wire
derivation: Ampère's law ∮B·dl = μ₀ I around a circle of radius r centred on the wire.
where_pi_enters: The length 2πr of the circular Ampère loop.

name: Reduced Planck constant
derivation: Planck's E = hν written in angular frequency ω = 2πν gives E = ħω.
where_pi_enters: Converting cycles to radians, ω = 2πν (one cycle is a full turn).

name: Simple pendulum period
derivation: Small-angle linearization gives θ'' = −(g/L)θ, simple harmonic motion with angular frequency √(g/L); the period is a full turn of phase.
where_pi_enters: One period is a phase advance of 2π in the solution cos(ωt).

name: Kepler's third law
derivation: For a circular orbit, equate gravity GMm/a² to the centripetal force m ω² a with ω = 2π/T, then square.
where_pi_enters: ω = 2π/T, one orbit being a full turn.

name: Einstein field equations coupling
derivation: Fix the coupling by requiring the weak-field, slow-motion limit to reproduce Poisson's equation ∇²Φ = 4πGρ.
where_pi_enters: Poisson's equation for Newtonian gravity, whose 4π is the area of the unit sphere from Gauss's law.

name: Stefan–Boltzmann integral
derivation: Expand 1/(eˣ − 1) = Σ e^{-nx}, integrate term by term to Γ(4)·ζ(4) = 6·π⁴/90.
where_pi_enters: The value ζ(4) = π⁴/90.

name: Maxwell–Boltzmann mean speed
derivation: Average v over the Maxwell speed distribution 4π (m/2πkT)^{3/2} v² e^{-mv²/2kT}; the v³ integral is elementary.
where_pi_enters: The normalization (m/2πkT)^{3/2}, from the three Gaussian integrals of the velocity components.

name: Hertzian dipole radiation resistance
derivation: Integrate the radiated power density of a short current element, proportional to sin²θ, over the sphere and divide by I²/2.
where_pi_enters: Integrating over the sphere: ∫dφ over 2π times ∫ sin³θ dθ = 4/3.

name: Effective aperture of an isotropic antenna
derivation: Combine G = 4π A_e/λ² (from the beam solid angle of an aperture) with gain 1 for an isotropic antenna, or a thermodynamic argument with a resistor in a blackbody cavity.
where_pi_enters: The full solid angle 4π of the sphere over which the isotropic antenna receives.
